summary: Andrew Goudie is an archaeologist and historian who was educated at Dean Close School and Trinity Hall (BA, MA, PhD 1964–1970). He served as Head and Professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.

Indologist Andrew Henry Yarrow earned his B.A. from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1934–1938) and his Ph.D. from Yale (~1946–1950) under Franklin Edgerton. He held posts at Yale, Columbia, and the University of Miami (Professor ~1968–1989).

Andrew Hollingworth Frost was an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed his B.A. at St John's College (1838–1842). He served as Principal of Church Missionary Society College (1870–1874) and Lecturer in Marathi and Gujarati at Cambridge (1884–1902).

Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Andrew J. Nicholson studied under the traditional teacher Sri Narayana Mishra. As of 2026, he is Associate Professor and Director of the Program in South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University.
Andrew Jukes was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Blundell's School. He served as a medical missionary for the Church Mission Society from 1878 to 1906.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Andrew Olendzki studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as Executive Director at the Insight Meditation Society, Executive Director and Resident Scholar at Barre Center for Buddhist Studies, and senior scholar at Mind and Life Institute.
Indologist and linguist Andrew Ollett studied at the University of Oxford (~2008–2010) and Columbia University (~2011–2017). He became an Associate Professor at the University of Chicago around 2023.

Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.
Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Andrew Quintman studied under Jay L. Garfield. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Linguist and Indologist Andrew Sihler studied at Harvard (~1958–1962) and Yale (~1962–1967) under doctoral supervisor Warren Crawford Cowgill. He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1967 to 1998.

Andrew Stirling was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied at East India Company College (1811–1812) and Fort William College (~1813–1814). He served in the East India Company's Political Department from around 1820 to 1830.

Specializing in Japanology and history/archaeology, Andrew Watsky studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1986–1994). He served on the faculty at Vassar College from around 1995 to 2008.

Andrew William Kennedy is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under doctoral supervisors Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Linguist and Indologist Andrey Klebanov earned his MA and Dr. Phil. at the University of Hamburg. He served as Professor at Kyoto University (2016–2021), University Assistant at the University of Vienna (2022–2026), and MSCA postdoctoral fellow at Hamburg (2026).

Andrey Terentyev, a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, studied philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University and completed his Ph.D. at the Russian Academy of Sciences. He held a post at the Museum of History of Religion (~1977–1988).
Andrey Zaliznyak studied under Vyacheslav Ivanov from around 1953 to 1958 and under André Martinet from around 1956 to 1957.

Indologist and linguist Andrzej Gawroński studied at the University of Lviv and University of Leipzig (PhD 1908). He held positions at Jagiellonian University, the University of Warsaw, and the University of Lviv as Professor of Indology (1917).

Indologist and linguist Andrzej Ługowski studied at Adam Mickiewicz University and the University of Warsaw (MA ~1956–1961), completing his doctorate under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz. He taught at the University of Warsaw from around 1961 to 2005.

A scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies, András Róna-Tas studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. He was Professor of Altaic Studies and Early Hungarian History at the University of Szeged (1968–2002).

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar André Bareau studied at the Sorbonne and EPHE under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at the CNRS, EPHE (Directeur d'Études 1956–1973), and Collège de France (Professor 1971–1991).
